title: Experiment Design: a reproducible plate plan and exact export
description: Edit a proposed plate layout through the actual controls, inspect capacity and replication warnings, reproduce random assignments and export the exact well map.
objectives: Plan conditions and control roles before acquisition.
Demonstrate warning and recovery states without treating layout checks as biological validation.
Reproduce the same random layout and distinguish selected wells from assigned conditions.
Export and retain the exact well table when row/column settings cannot express the design.
prerequisite: No acquired images or downloaded dataset are required for this planning module. The recording uses the application's real draft of six negative-control, six positive-control and twelve treatment wells, named tutorial_plan. These counts illustrate the interface; they are not a power calculation or acquired experimental result.

scenes.narration: Open Experiment Design in Home's Data category before acquisition. This module creates a proposed plate layout, not measured biological results. Our negative, positive and treatment names are draft labels; choose meaningful names and controls for your own experiment.

Name the plate so its identifier will match the images and measurements later. If a table column is narrow, double-click its header boundary to fit the contents. Review Condition, Replicates and Role together. The example's six, six and twelve wells demonstrate the interface, not a justified sample size.

Choosing a six-well format while requesting twenty-four wells produces a capacity error. The map does not quietly drop excess replicates. Read the message, then change the format or experimental plan; do not treat an empty map as a valid allocation.

Returning to ninety-six wells restores all twenty-four assignments. The plate map updates from the current table. Add condition and Remove selected manage condition rows; the square wells below are a separate selection surface, not those table rows.

Select a replicate cell and press F two to edit it. Reducing the negative control to one well raises a warning; restoring six removes that warning. Many cells within one well do not substitute for independent experimental replication.

Block layout places conditions together and raises positional-confounding warnings. Read these as prompts to inspect the design, not automatic biological conclusions. Optical illumination correction does not correct evaporation or temperature effects; experimental layout and image shading are different problems.

Choose random layout, leave edge empty, and seed forty-two. The outer ring leaves sixty usable wells on this ninety-six-well plate; our plan assigns twenty-four. Avoiding the outer ring costs capacity and does not guarantee freedom from all spatial effects.

Changing the seed to forty-three changes the actual assignments while preserving the requested condition counts. Randomisation reduces systematic placement bias, but a single random layout still needs review. Do not pick a seed to favour a desired outcome.

Returning to forty-two restores exactly the same well-to-condition mapping. Record the seed together with the plate format, edge policy and condition table. The seed alone does not define a design if those other inputs change.

Drag across B zero two to C zero four to select six wells. The selection outline changes, but their conditions do not: this gesture selects wells and does not assign a treatment. Check the condition table and the displayed map when revising an allocation.

Use Export plate map and choose a dedicated folder. The real export writes plate_map dot CSV, plate_map dot JSON and plate_map_settings dot JSON. Keep the three files together; selecting a destination is not the same as acquiring the planned experiment.

The CSV contains one row per assigned well: twenty-four here, matching every displayed condition and role. It joins to measurements using plate I D, row I D and column I D together. The JSON records the seed, design and findings, including warnings rather than hiding them.

This random layout cannot be represented by the row-or-column treatment settings. The settings file explicitly reports expressible as false; it is not a complete analysis configuration. Use the exact exported well table and an explicit join, rather than approximating mixed wells with whole-row labels.

The Python interface lives in spacr.qt.widgets.plate_layout: Condition and PlateDesign describe the plan; assign_wells, check_design and write_design allocate, inspect and save it. Layout checks do not establish statistical power or biological validity. Review the design before acquisition and keep its exact map for downstream analysis.
